extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (attorneys/agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on when a first Office action may be made final (including in continuations, RCEs, CPAs), rules on withdrawing finality, timing and processing of replies after final, examiner amendments, and transitional after-final practice under 37 CFR 1.129.

rubrics_metrics.name: First-action final rejection in continuing/substitute application (conditions A & B)
rubrics_metrics.description: A first Office action may be made final when (A) the new application is a continuing application of, or a substitute for, an earlier application, and all claims of the new application (1) are identical to, patentably indistinct from, or have unity of invention with, the claims in the earlier application (i.e., restriction would not have been proper if the new or amended claims had been entered in the earlier application), and (2) would have been properly finally rejected on the grounds and art of record in the next Office action if they had been entered in the earlier application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.41 (Action Is Final, First Action) to make a first-action final rejection in such cases. Remind applicant of 37 CFR 1.136(a) extension policy. Examiner notes: do not use this form paragraph if an amendment was refused entry in the parent case because it raised new issues or new matter (see MPEP § 706.07(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: First-action final rejection following RCE (conditions A & B)
rubrics_metrics.description: For an application in which an RCE has been filed, claims may be finally rejected in the first action following the filing of the RCE (with a submission and fee under 37 CFR 1.114) when all the claims in the application after the entry of the submission under 37 CFR 1.114 and any entered supplemental amendments (A) are identical to, patentably indistinct from, or have unity of invention with the claims in the application prior to the entry of the submission under 37 CFR 1.114 (i.e., restriction would not have been proper if the new or amended claims had been entered prior to the filing of the RCE), and (B) would have been properly finally rejected on the grounds and art of record in the next Office action if they had been entered in the application prior to the filing of the RCE under 37 CFR 1.114.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note that applicants cannot use an RCE to obtain continued examination on the basis of claims that are independent and distinct from, or lack unity of invention with, the claims previously claimed and examined as a matter of right (i.e., applicant cannot switch inventions). See 37 CFR 1.145 and MPEP § 706.07(h). Condition (A) is always met where the RCE is accompanied by a submission that will be entered as a matter of right.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not make final where previously refused entry raised new issues or new matter
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not proper to make final a first Office action in a continuing or substitute application where that application contains material which was presented in the earlier application after final rejection or closing of prosecution but was denied entry because (A) new issues were raised that required further consideration and/or search, or (B) the issue of new matter was raised. Similarly, it would not be proper to make final a first Office action after the filing of an RCE where material was presented after final rejection or closing of prosecution and prior to the filing of the RCE, but was denied entry because (A) new issues were raised that required further consideration and/or search, or (B) the issue of new matter was raised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an amendment was refused entry in the parent case on the grounds that it raised new issues or new matter, the form paragraph for first-action-final cannot be used. See MPEP § 706.07(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuation-in-part (CIP) cannot be first-action-final if claims include new matter
rubrics_metrics.description: It would not be proper to make final a first Office action in a continuation-in-part application where any claim includes subject matter not present in the earlier application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that claims in a CIP do not introduce new subject matter relative to the parent if considering a first-action final rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews prior to first action in continuing/substitute apps
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for an interview prior to first action on a continuing or substitute application should ordinarily be granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grant interviews as part of examiner practice to assist in resolving issues before making a first-action final rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of form paragraphs for first-action final rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: A first action final rejection should be made by using Form Paragraphs 7.41 or 7.41.03, as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific form paragraphs exist for various scenarios (e.g., 7.41, 7.41.03 for CPAs/design, 7.42.09 for RCE first-action final). Use the paragraph appropriate to the factual situation and insert required bracketed items per Examiner Notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prematureness of a final rejection must be raised while application pending
rubrics_metrics.description: Any question as to prematureness of a final rejection should be raised, if at all, while the application is still pending before the primary examiner. This is a question of practice, distinct from the tenability of the rejection. It may not be advanced as a ground for appeal or made the basis of complaint before the PTAB; it is reviewable by petition under 37 CFR 1.181.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timeliness: raise prematureness issues during pendency; rely on petition when necessary. See MPEP § 1002.02(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of finality when final rejection is premature
rubrics_metrics.description: If, on request by applicant for reconsideration, the primary examiner finds the final rejection to have been premature, he or she should withdraw the finality of the rejection. The finality of the Office action must be withdrawn while the application is still pending. The examiner cannot withdraw the final rejection once the application is abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once finality is withdrawn, the next Office action may be made final if conditions of MPEP § 706.07(a) are met. Use form paragraph 7.42 when withdrawing finality of the last Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: General limits on withdrawal of final rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a final rejection that is not premature has been entered in an application/reexamination proceeding, it should not be withdrawn at the applicant’s or patent owner’s request except on a showing under 37 CFR 1.116(b). Further amendment or argument will be considered in certain instances. An amendment that will place the application either in condition for allowance or in better form for appeal may be admitted. Also, amendments complying with objections or requirements as to form are to be permitted after final action in accordance with 37 CFR 1.116(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner may withdraw the rejection of finally rejected claims if new facts or reasons are presented convincing that the claims are allowable or patentable (including reexamination). Withdrawal to apply a new ground of rejection is permissible but limited to situations where a new reference fully meets at least one claim or meets it except for differences shown to be completely obvious. Do not use withdrawal for subsidiary/cumulative references or those merely 'better than' those of record. When a final rejection is withdrawn, amendments filed after the final rejection are ordinarily entered. New grounds of rejection made when reopening prosecution after an appeal brief require SPE approval. See MPEP § 1207.03 and § 1002.02(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time-for-reply rules and shortened statutory period (SSP) mechanics
rubrics_metrics.description: All final rejections setting a 3-month shortened statutory period for reply should contain an appropriate form paragraph advising applicant that if the first reply is filed within 2 months of the date of the final Office action, the shortened statutory period will expire at 3 months from the date of the final rejection or on the date the advisory action is mailed, whichever is later. In no event can the statutory period for reply expire later than 6 months from the mailing date of the final action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List of form paragraphs to be used when setting a 3-month SSP is provided. If the last day of the 2-month period falls on a weekend/holiday and reply is filed on the next business day, reply is deemed timely. The procedure doesn't apply where SSP < 3 months (e.g., reissue litigation or reexamination). See MPEP § 710.05 and other cross-references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory action duties when applicant files first reply within 2 months
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the final Office action sets a variable reply period and applicant files a complete first reply within 2 months, the examiner must determine if the reply: (1) places the application in condition for allowance — then process as allowance and no extension fees; (2) places the application in condition for allowance except for matters of form which the examiner can change without authorization from applicant — then amend and process as allowance and no extension fees; or (3) does not place the application in condition for allowance — then the advisory action should inform applicant that the SSP for reply expires 3 months from the date of the final rejection or as of the mailing date of the advisory action, whichever is later, by checking box 1.b) on PTOL-303.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the first reply within 2 months results in allowance (or allowance except for formal matters), process without extension fees. If not, mail advisory action informing applicant of the SSP expiration accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing when applicant does NOT file complete first reply within 2 months
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the final Office action sets a variable reply period and applicant does NOT file a complete first reply within 2 months, examiners should check box 1.a) at the top portion of the Advisory Action form, PTOL-303.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checking PTOL-303 box 1.a) places applicant on notice that they did not reply in the 2-month window and the variable timing rules apply accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: When advisory action box 1.b is checked — timing and extension fee calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: When box 1.b) on PTOL-303 is checked, the time for applicant to take further action (including calculation of extension fees under 37 CFR 1.136(a)) begins to run 3 months from the date of the final rejection, or from the date of the advisory action, whichever is later. Extension fees cannot be prorated for portions of a month. In no event can the statutory period for reply expire later than 6 months from the date of the final rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an advisory action is mailed after the 3-month period, the SSP will expire on the date the advisory action is mailed, and extension fees are calculated from that mailing date. Example scenarios and cross-references provided (MPEP § 710.01(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's amendments after a first reply within 2 months
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a complete first reply to a final Office action has been filed within 2 months, an examiner’s amendment to place the application in condition for allowance may be made without the payment of extension fees even if the examiner’s amendment is made more than 3 months from the date of the final Office action. Note that an examiner’s amendment may not be made more than 6 months from the date of the final Office action, as the application would be abandoned at that point by operation of law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make examiner's amendments to place app in condition for allowance without extension fees if first reply was timely (within 2 months). Do not make examiner amendments after 6 months from final OA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's amendments when no timely first reply — applicant authorization required
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a complete first reply to a final Office action has not been filed within 2 months of the final Office action, applicant’s authorization to make an amendment to place the application in condition for allowance must be made either within the 3-month shortened statutory period or within an extended period for reply that has been petitioned and paid for by applicant pursuant to 37 CFR 1.136(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner's amendment correcting only formal matters identified for the first time after a reply would not require any extension fee, since the reply put the application in condition for allowance except for the correction of formal matters which had not yet been required by the examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of time procedures and authorization requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An extension of time under 37 CFR 1.136(a) requires a petition for an extension and the appropriate fee under 37 CFR 1.17. Where an extension is necessary to place an application in condition for allowance (e.g., when an examiner’s amendment is necessary after the shortened statutory period has expired), applicant may file the required petition and fee or give authorization to the examiner to make the petition of record and charge a specified fee to a deposit account. Office employees may not accept oral (telephonic) instructions to complete credit card payments or otherwise charge a patent process fee to a credit card. When authorization to make a petition for an extension of time of record is given to the examiner, the authorization must be given before the extended period expires and must be made of record in an examiner’s amendment by indicating the name of the person making the authorization, when the authorization was given, the deposit account number to be charged, the length of the extension requested and the amount of the fee to be charged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Form Paragraph 13.02.02 (Extension of Time and Examiner’s Amendment Authorized) to document authorizations. Ensure authorization entry requirements are met to permit examiner to charge deposit account and file petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice after final — processing and limits on considering replies
rubrics_metrics.description: Replies after final should be processed and considered promptly by all Office personnel. Replies after final should not be considered by the examiner unless they are filed within the SSP or are accompanied by a petition for an extension of time and the appropriate fee (37 CFR 1.17 and 37 CFR 1.136(a)). This requirement also applies to supplemental replies filed after the first reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interviews may be conducted after expiration of the SSP but within the 6-month statutory period for reply without payment of an extension fee. Formal matters identified for the first time after a reply and that require action by applicant to correct may be required in an Ex parte Quayle action if the application is otherwise in condition for allowance (no extension fees). If prosecution is to be reopened after a final Office action has been replied to, the finality of the previous Office action should be withdrawn to avoid abandonment and the payment of extension fees. Form paragraph 7.42 may be used in addition to a statement withdrawing finality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitional after-final practice (37 CFR 1.129) eligibility and effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 37 CFR 1.129, an applicant in an application (other than reissue or design) pending for at least two years as of June 8, 1995 (taking into account any reference to earlier-filed applications under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121, 365(c)) is entitled to have a first submission entered and considered on the merits after final rejection if the first submission and the fee under 37 CFR 1.17(r) are filed prior to the filing of an appeal brief and prior to abandonment. The finality of the final rejection is automatically withdrawn upon timely filing of the submission and payment of the fee. A second submission with payment is available under the same timing constraints if a subsequent final rejection is made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 'submission' includes IDS, amendments to written description/claims/drawings, a new substantive argument, or new evidence. No amendment considered as a result of payment of the fee may introduce new matter (35 U.S.C. 132). This transitional practice does not apply to applications filed after June 8, 1995, and is not available for reissue, design applications, or reexamination proceedings. Use form paragraph 7.41.01.fti to notify applicant when application qualifies under 37 CFR 1.129(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph and notice requirements for transitional after-final practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph 7.41.01.fti may be used to notify applicant that the application qualifies under 37 CFR 1.129(a). The submission under 37 CFR 1.129(a) may comprise, but is not limited to, an IDS, an amendment to the written description, claims or drawings, a new substantive argument and/or new evidence. No amendment considered as a result of payment of the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(r) may introduce new matter into the disclosure of the application (35 U.S.C. 132).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant has filed multiple proposed amendments which, when entered, would conflict with one another, provide specific instructions for entry or non-entry of each amendment upon payment of any fee under 37 CFR 1.17(r). Do not use this paragraph for design, reissue, or reexamination applications.
